transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 mins
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Li (Redwood SE), Alex Monroe (Orion Head of Platform), Sara Iqbal (ML Eng), Priya Desai (Security), Tom R. (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick final preflight for pilot -> discussion of canary sizing, instrumentation, cutover steps, rollback criteria, and last-mile security checks. Agreement to run a 24h canary at 10% traffic on dedicated pool and for Redwood to send a compact cutover runbook.

Topics:
- Canary size and traffic gating
- A/B vs straight canary for safety and user-experience metrics
- Telemetry + alert thresholds (latency p95, error rate, hallucination rate proxy)
- Rollback conditions and automation hooks
- Security: KMS, audit logs, retention, and SOC2 checklist items
- Runbook owners and on-call rotation for launch window

----- Transcript -----
[00:00] Maya: all right everyone i think we can get started, thanks for making time. quick check, audio okay?
[00:07] Alex: yeah loud and clear, thanks Maya.
[00:10] Maya: perfect. Today is the preflight, so goal is pick a go/no go date, run through canary/ab options, hammer out cutover steps and owners. Jordan will run through the perf numbers first.
[00:23] Jordan: cool. so since last week we ran the 1h spike tests with a synthetic workload approximating your median session length — we saw p95 at about 310ms on the dedicated gpus, tail spikes to 480ms under simulated 3x burst. average token cost was about $0.0019 per token equivalent in our measurement with the quantized variant. note there was a mismatch in batch sizing between our harness and your staging small service, so i'm going to re-run a 24h with the same batching profile you have in prod.
[00:53] Sara: wait can you repeat the quantized variant number? i thought earlier you said 0.0028.
[00:58] Jordan: yeah, so 0.0019 was after enabling int8-style quantization and the optimized kernels for long context. the 0.0028 is the baseline float16 profile, so if you prefer "closest to reference" quality we can stick with f16 and expect slightly higher cost.
[01:20] Tom R.: do we lose quality significantly with int8-ish? we're worried about radiology notes where hallucinations are sensitive.
[01:28] Jordan: good call. the quality diffs are small on typical prompts but for edge-case clinically-sensitive templates we recommend running targeted evals — we've got Redwood Optimize suggestions that will surface prompt-sensitive regressions. sara can run sample prompts in the canary and we'll measure divergence.
[01:45] Priya: on encryption, we need KMS integration for key rotation, and audit logs for every inference request metadata that touches PHI. is that supported in the dedicated offering?
[01:56] Maya: yes, dedicated supports customer-managed KMS keys and audit log export. Jordan can show the flow — it's a config you enable in the private control plane and logs stream to your SIEM via our log forwarder.
[02:08] Jordan: that's right. small nit — currently the export includes request metadata; payload-level PHI masking is up to you at the app layer. but we do have request-level trace IDs and token consumption logs.
[02:22] Alex: okay, good. Now about the canary: we were thinking 5% traffic for 48h, but after seeing the burst tests 10% for 24h sounds reasonable to catch tail latency and regression. thoughts?
[02:35] Maya: 10% for 24h is a good compromise — captures peak hours across your EU/US overlap and short enough if we need to rollback. Jordan, what metrics do you want to gate on?
[02:45] Jordan: p95 latency, error rate (5xx and SDK client errors), a simple hallucination proxy — we can use a quality scorer on a prompt set and watch delta vs baseline; also token cost and CPU/GPU mem pressure. We'll set thresholds: p95 > 450ms or error rate up 2x baseline -> auto-fail. hallucination delta > 4% on the seed prompts -> manual review.
[03:08] Sara: can we automate rollback on p95 spikes? I want automation for immediate rollback if we cross threshold during a peak.
[03:15] Jordan: yes, Redwood's routing policy can auto-fallback to previous model variant or to hosted low-cost fallback. but for production safety we usually do auto-fallback to the last-known-good variant and page the on-call. we will wire the webhook to your orchestration so you have the final kill switch.
[03:31] Priya: about A/B — is there a reason to do A/B vs canary? we are concerned about product metrics — i.e., conversion on a triage flow.
[03:40] Maya: A/B gives you clean signal for business metrics but it's more invasive and requires instrumentation in the product to split traffic and measure. Canary is simpler operationally. For your use-case since there are high-sensitivity prompts, I'd recommend a canary to validate infra and telemetry, then a short A/B for UX/metric verification if infra stability looks good.
[03:59] Alex: timeline wise we want go/no-go by next week. If we run the 24h canary starting 12/23 UTC, we could meet a soft launch 12/30 pending successful telemetry.
[04:11] Jordan: sounds feasible. I'll schedule the canary in the morning window 02:00 UTC to capture your US/EMEA overlap.
[04:18] Tom R: what about rollout steps — who is owner for switching traffic?
[04:21] Maya: Maya: ops step owner is Alex for cutover approval, Jordan will execute the route shift, Tom will monitor infra alerts, Priya will sign off on security checklist. I'll send the runbook and the slim on-call matrix.
[04:35] Alex: noted. can you be specific on rollback play? like how long do we wait after we see a spike before flipping back?
[04:42] Jordan: recommended pattern: immediate auto-fallback for infra errors or p95 > threshold; for hallucination regression we do a manual rollback after a quick 30-minute investigation window. we'll surface the relevant logs and sample transcripts to the triage dashboard.
[04:56] Sara: question on telemetry retention. We need 90 days of token-level billing for audits, but aggregated latency/slo metrics can be shorter. How does Redwood handle retention tiers?
[05:06] Maya: retention is configurable. billing/token logs can be exported to your storage for 90+ days. aggregated metrics in Console are 30 days by default but we can enable longer windows as an add-on.
[05:18] Priya: one more compliance item: we need per-request audit trail for egress to third-party telemetry. Make sure the trace ID is present in every forwarded log.
[05:27] Jordan: that's in place — trace IDs are injected and the forwarder includes them. we'll share a sample log line in the runbook.
[05:33] Alex: ok good. switching to runbook specifics — Maya, can you walk through the cutover steps you plan to send?
[05:39] Maya: sure. the cutover doc will be: pre-cut checks (health, backup, test seed set), canary configuration (traffic %, start time), monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds, escalation matrix, rollback commands and automation webhooks, post-cut checks and verification script. short, 2-page checklist plus a playbook appendix.
[05:57] Tom R: will the post-cut smoke tests include a burst replay?
[06:01] Jordan: yes, we'll replay representative session logs through the canary route and run the QA scorer. also we'll run a few synthetic long-context sessions to validate KV cache behavior — note sometimes transcripts call it K V cache and some tools mangle that word.
[06:18] Sara: small nit — we need to ensure the scorer doesn't leak PHI. use anonymized examples.
[06:23] Jordan: absolutely. we'll use hashed tokens and masked prompts.
[06:27] Maya: good call. anyone object to the 10% x 24h canary start time?
[06:31] Alex: no objections.
[06:33] Priya: none.
[06:34] Maya: ok we'll proceed. next, question about dedicated pool autoscaling on a canary — do we let it autoscale?
[06:41] Jordan: for the canary we lock a minimum and a small burst cap, so that autoscaling doesn't hide a perf regression. you want the canary to reflect realistic headroom but not infinite scale. we'll set min=2 nodes, max=6 nodes for the 10% test.
[06:56] Sara: how about AB percent — if we later choose to run an A/B, what are recommended split sizes?
[07:01] Jordan: typically 50/50 for a short 1-2 day A/B yields clean metrics but higher risk. for a cautious A/B you can do 20/80 and look for delta signals.
[07:11] Alex: a few admin items — we need the final runbook in the next 48 hours, and we should schedule a final preflight with legal and incident commander present on 12/29.
[07:22] Maya: will do. Jordan will post the logs link and cost summary to the shared drive.
[07:27] Jordan: yep i'll attach the perf logs and the Optimize recommendations sheet — there's a small suggestion to change batch_size from 8 to 12 for this workload to reduce token latency by ~8% without changing quality.
[07:40] Sara: If we change batch size, will it change token costs?
[07:43] Jordan: slightly — batching improves throughput so marginal cost per token can drop, but per-request latency profile changes. that's why we test in canary.
[07:52] Priya: last sec security question — do you support HSM-backed KMS or only cloud KMS?
[07:58] Maya: dedicated can be configured to talk to customer HSM via our connector; we'll include setup steps in the security appendix.
[08:05] Alex: great. any blockers?
[08:08] Sara: none from ML except I need the seed prompts validated.
[08:12] Priya: none after we get the KMS policy doc.
[08:14] Tom R: I'll monitor infra and confirm alert hooks.
[08:16] Maya: awesome. recap: Jordan runs 24h canary starting 2026-12-23 02:00 UTC at 10% traffic; Maya sends runbook by 12/24; Priya reviews KMS/compliance by 12/28; final preflight on 12/29 with legal and incident commander.
[08:32] Alex: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:34] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links.
[08:37] Jordan: i'll ping the drive after this call.
[08:40] End of meeting.
